definition: A substance that cannot be split into anything simpler by chemical means; all its atoms have the same atomic number.
msAccepts: made of only one type of atom
cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means
all atoms have the same atomic number
msAvoids: can be separated by filtering or heating

definition: Two or more elements chemically combined, always in fixed proportions; it can only be split apart by chemical reactions.
msAccepts: two or more elements chemically combined
in fixed proportions
cannot be separated by physical means

definition: Two or more substances (elements and/or compounds) mixed together with no chemical reaction; the components can be in any proportion and keep their own properties.
msAccepts: not chemically combined
components in any proportion
components keep their own properties
can be separated by physical means

definition: The smallest neutral particle of an element; the building block shown in element and compound diagrams. (Full structure: Chapter 3.)
msAccepts: smallest particle of an element
msAvoids: smallest particle of anything (that is not what IGCSE claims)

definition: The number of protons in the nucleus of an atom. All atoms of the same element share the same atomic number.
msAccepts: number of protons (in the nucleus)
same atomic number means same element
msAvoids: number of particles in the atom

definition: Atoms of the same element with the same atomic number but different mass numbers, because they contain different numbers of neutrons.
msAccepts: same protons, different neutrons
same atomic number, different mass number

definition: The chart displaying all 118 elements; most occur naturally, a few are made artificially.
msAccepts: arrangement of all the elements

definition: The fixed ratio of atoms in a compound written with symbols and subscript numbers, e.g. HF, MgF₂, CO₂, CH₄.
msAccepts: shows the elements and the fixed ratio of atoms in a compound

definition: A single element or single compound, with nothing else mixed in; it melts and boils at fixed temperatures.
msAccepts: only one substance present
fixed/sharp melting and boiling point

definition: An unwanted substance mixed with the one you want; impurities lower the melting point and raise the boiling point of a substance.
msAccepts: unwanted substance present in a sample
lowers melting point / raises boiling point

definition: The fixed temperature at which a pure solid melts; impurities lower it and make melting happen over a range.
msAccepts: temperature at which a solid melts
pure substances melt at a fixed temperature

definition: The fixed temperature at which a pure liquid boils; impurities raise it, so a solution boils above 100 °C.
msAccepts: temperature at which a liquid boils
pure liquids boil at a fixed temperature
msAvoids: when bubbles appear at any temperature

definition: Separating an insoluble solid from a liquid by pouring through filter paper; the solid left is the residue, the liquid passing through is the filtrate.
msAccepts: residue left on filter paper
filtrate passes through
separates insoluble solid from liquid
msAvoids: the salt is caught by the paper

definition: The solid left on the filter paper after filtration.
msAccepts: solid left on the filter paper

definition: The liquid that passes through the filter paper during filtration.
msAccepts: liquid that comes through the filter paper

definition: Separating a solute from its solution by evaporating solvent until the solution is nearly saturated, then cooling so crystals form; crystals are filtered off.
msAccepts: heat to evaporate solvent until nearly saturated
crystals form on cooling
tested with a glass rod

definition: A solution holding the maximum amount of dissolved solute at that temperature; crystals form on its surface or on a dipped glass rod.
msAccepts: contains the maximum dissolved solute at that temperature
no more solute can dissolve

definition: Separating the solvent from a solution: the solvent boils, is condensed in the condenser and collected, while dissolved solids stay in the flask.
msAccepts: solvent evaporates then condenses
collect the water; salt stays in the flask
msAvoids: the salt evaporates and is collected

definition: Separating a mixture of miscible liquids using their different boiling points in a fractionating column, e.g. ethanol (78 °C) from water (100 °C).
msAccepts: different boiling points
liquid with lower boiling point reaches the top of the column first
msAvoids: used to separate salt from water (that is simple distillation)

definition: Describes liquids that mix completely in any proportion to form a single layer, e.g. ethanol and water.
msAccepts: mix in any proportion forming one layer
msAvoids: liquids that don't mix (that is immiscible)

definition: The starting line on chromatography paper, drawn in pencil about 1 cm from the bottom, where spots are placed.
msAccepts: pencil line where spots are added
pencil (not pen) so it does not dissolve and move
msAvoids: drawn at the very bottom edge in the solvent

definition: The highest level the solvent reaches on the chromatography paper before the run is stopped.
msAccepts: furthest point reached by the solvent
mark the solvent front before it reaches the top
msAvoids: where the dye spots end up

definition: The pattern of spots left on the chromatography paper after the solvent has moved up and the paper has dried.
msAccepts: the pattern of spots produced by chromatography
used to identify the components of a mixture

definition: Distance moved by a spot divided by distance moved by the solvent front, both measured from the pencil line; always between 0 and 1, with no units.
msAccepts: distance moved by substance ÷ distance moved by solvent front
no units
measure to the centre of the spot
msAvoids: measured to the edge of the spot
